rationale: Use a broad scouting gradient to locate all 10 compounds and identify the limiting pairs near the target run time. A midrange temperature leaves room to adjust selectivity in either direction.

Lengthen only the gradient to test whether the two limiting pairs respond to slope. The current last peak at 7.16 minutes leaves room to improve resolution while aiming to keep all peaks within 10 minutes.

The limiting pair improved strongly with a shallower gradient. Narrowing the solvent window provides further slope reduction, while raising the starting organic fraction should help keep the last peak within 10 minutes.

Narrow the gradient window further to raise the remaining limiting resolution from 1.42 toward full credit. The higher starting organic fraction should offset the shallower slope enough to keep the last peak below 10 minutes, while the early peaks have ample separation.

Injection 4 already achieves the maximum CRF and remains the benchmark. Increase temperature by 5 °C to test whether the run can be shortened while preserving full resolution, especially the limiting pair at R = 1.58.

Retain injection 4 as the maximum-score benchmark. Test a substantially higher temperature to move beyond the close-pair convergence seen at 45 °C, combined with a shorter gradient to search for a faster fully resolved method.

Test whether a steeper gradient separates the new limiting pair at 60 °C by shifting relative retention. This also explores a faster method, while injection 4 remains the established maximum-score fallback.

Shift the solvent window lower while preserving the gradient slope from injection 7 to test starting-composition selectivity for the limiting pair. The 5.40-minute last peak leaves ample time for the added retention, and the lower start should improve early-peak retention.

Lowering the starting organic fraction worsened the limiting pair, so test a higher window at the same slope as injection 7. This may achieve full resolution in a shorter run, although compression of the first two peaks must be checked.

Explore lower-temperature selectivity with a shorter gradient than the fully resolved benchmark. This tests a different route to separating the central cluster after the high-temperature trials introduced new limiting pairs.

Test an intermediate high temperature to move the limiting pair seen at 60 °C away from convergence while retaining a short run. Holding the solvent program identical to injection 6 isolates the temperature effect.

The close pair appears to reverse order between 55 and 60 °C, so the lower starting composition that worsened its separation at 60 °C may improve it at 55 °C. Preserve injection 11’s gradient slope to test this selectivity shift, with ample time remaining below 10 minutes.

Injection 12 achieves maximum CRF with a shorter elution time than injection 4. Shorten only the gradient to test whether full resolution can be retained in an even faster run, monitoring both the 1.84 and 1.50 resolution pairs.

Use a slope between those of injections 12 and 13, targeting R ≥ 1.5 for both limiting pairs with a last peak earlier than 8.03 minutes. The lower endpoint should still accommodate the observed elution window.

Raise the starting fraction one grid step while keeping the endpoint and duration fixed to seek earlier elution. The resulting shallower slope may offset the starting-composition effect on the close middle pair, while improving the other limiting separation.

Return to the fully resolved 40 °C selectivity and shift the gradient window upward while preserving injection 4’s slope. This tests whether the higher starting fraction can shorten elution without losing resolution of the early peaks or central cluster.

Explore the untested 50 °C selectivity with a steeper gradient, seeking a faster fully resolved separation. The lower starting fraction protects early retention, while the steeper slope may separate the central pair that converged near 45 °C.

Reduce the slope slightly from injection 15 to lift its sole unresolved pair above R = 1.5 while retaining the favorable 55 °C selectivity. This targets a maximum-score method with more balanced resolution margins, though the final peak may elute during the hold.

Test the unexamined 35 °C selectivity with a shorter gradient than the 40 °C benchmark. A modest temperature reduction may improve its limiting central pair without the extensive crowding observed at 25 °C.

Use a gradient slope between injections 15 and 18 to target full resolution with more balanced margins than injection 14. This should shorten elution relative to injection 18 while keeping its limiting middle pair above R = 1.5.

Test a higher starting fraction with a shallower gradient to seek larger resolution margins at the maximum CRF. The slope reduction should compensate for the middle-pair compression seen when increasing the starting fraction, while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

Reduce the slope slightly from injection 21 to bring its sole limiting pair above R = 1.5. The last peak at 8.54 minutes leaves some room for added retention, potentially yielding full credit with larger separation margins than the faster methods.

Test a slope between injections 15 and 20 to locate the fastest fully resolved boundary at this starting composition. The limiting pair is predicted to lie near R = 1.5, with slightly earlier final elution than injection 20.

Test a slightly shallower slope than injection 22 to balance its two closest separations near R = 1.7. The last peak should remain below 10 minutes, targeting greater resolution margin while preserving the already-achieved maximum CRF.

Use a slope between injections 22 and 24 to balance the two limiting resolutions near 1.7 while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes. The maximum CRF is already secured; this final trial targets additional separation margin.
